Status: experimental; instruction-only.

## Triggers

Use when the user asks to:
- Aggregate single-cell RNA-seq counts into biological-replicate pseudobulks.
- Prepare cell-type-specific counts and metadata for bulk differential expression.
- Audit whether donor identity, repeated measures, or cell yields support a
  proposed pseudobulk comparison.

clustering, annotation, or differential abundance alone.

Prepare an aggregation specification, evidence audit, and handoff contract.
Do not assume Python, R, a shell, packages, file access, or any execution runtime.
If execution is unavailable, provide specifications and clearly label all
uncomputed quantities.

Use biological replicates as the units of inference. Cells and technical
libraries do not supply independent biological replication.

For standard count-based pseudobulk, sum verified unnormalized gene-level
counts within each intended biological sample and cell type. Retain donor,
condition, time point, tissue, and other relevant sample distinctions.
Do not aggregate across conditions merely because donor identity matches.

Do not sum normalized, log-transformed, scaled, integrated, or imputed values
and label the result raw-count pseudobulk. Do not round transformed values
to manufacture counts. Route alternative measurement types to a separately
justified method.

Merge technical partitions only when metadata establishes that they represent
the same intended biological sample and have compatible features and count
semantics. Never count those partitions as independent donors.

Do not perform normalization, differential-expression fitting, hypothesis
testing, or pathway analysis here. Hand those tasks to the bulk differential
expression skill, preserving this skill's design constraints.

## Evidence gates

For each gate, record PASS, BLOCKED, or NOT ASSESSED, with supporting evidence.
A prose specification does not establish that a data-dependent gate passed.

1. Measurement provenance
   Verify the assay/layer, count semantics, feature identifiers, and orientation.
   A layer named "counts" alone is insufficient evidence.
   Block count aggregation if provenance is unresolved.

2. Cell-to-sample mapping
   Require a unique cell identifier and a defensible mapping to biological
   sample, donor, cell type, and requested comparison variables.
   Report missing, duplicated, or conflicting assignments.
   Never infer donor identities from barcode text without a documented mapping.

3. Replication and design
   Tabulate independent donors by condition within each cell type.
   Identify paired samples, repeated observations, technical partitions,
   confounding, and missing combinations.
   One donor per condition cannot support population-level inference.
   Two donors is not an automatic adequacy threshold.
   Repeated-donor designs require an explicit compatible downstream model;
   do not assume a donor covariate always resolves dependence.
   Complete condition–batch confounding blocks that contrast.

4. Aggregation eligibility
   Specify grouping keys and justify any merging.
   State cell-quality exclusions and cell-type label provenance.
   Propose and justify minimum-cell and library-size criteria before reviewing
   differential-expression outcomes; there is no universal valid cutoff.
   Keep a record of excluded sample–cell-type combinations.

5. Output integrity
   If execution evidence exists, verify nonnegative count values, unique
   pseudobulk identifiers, exact count-column/metadata-row alignment,
   feature consistency, and count-sum conservation over retained cells.
   Investigate all-zero libraries.
   Distinguish an unobserved cell type from a measured zero expression value:
   do not fabricate all-zero pseudobulks for absent combinations.

6. Handoff readiness
   Reassess replication and design after exclusions, separately per cell type.
   Document unresolved gates and unsupported contrasts.
   Preparation may remain useful even when inferential analysis is blocked.
   Never describe a blocked contrast as ready for differential expression.

- Gene-by-pseudobulk count matrix, separately addressable by cell type.
- Exactly aligned metadata containing pseudobulk ID, biological sample ID,

- Cells contributing to each pseudobulk and library-size summaries.
- Inclusion/exclusion ledger, aggregation keys, provenance, and gate results.
- Intended contrast, pairing/dependence constraints, and confounding findings.

Have the bulk differential expression workflow verify count compatibility,
